to_digit.title: How char::to_digit works
to_digit.description: The number a digit character stands for, in a given base.

slides.caption: A char like '7' is not the number 7. to_digit converts it.
'x' is not a digit in base 10: None.
Summing the digits of a string: s.chars().filter_map(|c| c.to_digit(10)).sum::<u32>().

from_digit.title: How char::from_digit works
from_digit.description: The digit character for a number, in a given base.

slides.caption: from_digit turns a small number into the character that writes it.
A number too big for the base, like from_digit(10, 10), gives None.

is_alphabetic.title: How char::is_alphabetic works
is_alphabetic.description: true for letters, in any alphabet.

slides.caption: is_alphabetic follows Unicode, so letters with accents and other alphabets count.
'1' is a digit, not a letter.
is_ascii_alphabetic only accepts a–z and A–Z.
is_alphanumeric is true for anything that is a letter or a number.
Common for cleaning input: keep only letters and digits.

is_whitespace.title: How char::is_whitespace works
is_whitespace.description: true for spaces, tabs, newlines and other blank characters.

slides.caption: is_whitespace recognises every kind of blank character, not just the space.
split_whitespace and trim use exactly this test.

to_ascii_uppercase.title: How char::to_ascii_uppercase works
to_ascii_uppercase.description: Uppercases a–z; every other character stays the same.

slides.caption: to_ascii_uppercase only touches the 26 ASCII letters and always returns exactly one char.
'é' is not ASCII, so it is returned unchanged.
char::to_uppercase follows Unicode instead and can give several characters ('ß' → "SS").

len_utf8.title: How char::len_utf8 works
len_utf8.description: How many bytes the character takes in a UTF-8 string.

slides.caption: UTF-8 uses 1 byte for ASCII and up to 4 bytes for other characters.
This is why String::len() (bytes) and chars().count() (characters) can differ.

is_ascii_digit.title: How char::is_ascii_digit works
is_ascii_digit.description: true only for the characters 0 to 9.

slides.caption: is_numeric also accepts other kinds of numerals (like Roman numeral characters); for parsing numbers, is_ascii_digit is usually what you want.

is_numeric.title: How char::is_numeric works
is_numeric.description: true for numeric characters, including ones beyond 0–9.

slides.caption: is_numeric follows Unicode: fractions and other numerals count too.
Before parsing, is_ascii_digit is usually the better test: "½".parse::<u32>() fails.

to_uppercase.title: How char::to_uppercase works
to_uppercase.description: An iterator of the upper-case form, which can be more than one char.

slides.caption: to_uppercase returns an iterator because some letters become several.
to_ascii_uppercase always returns exactly one char, but only changes a–z.

from_u32.title: How char::from_u32 works
from_u32.description: The char with a given Unicode number, if it is a valid character.

slides.caption: Every char has a number (its code point). Not every number is a char.
The other way: 'A' as u32 is 65.

char.title: How parse works for char
char.description: Turns a string of exactly one character into a char.

slides.caption: The string must contain exactly one char (it may be several bytes long).
Two characters, or none, is an error.
s.chars().next() gets the first char of any string instead.

is_lowercase.title: How char::is_lowercase works
is_lowercase.description: true for lower-case letters, in any alphabet.

slides.caption: Unlike is_ascii_lowercase, letters like é and ß count.

to_lowercase.title: How char::to_lowercase works
to_lowercase.description: An iterator of the lower-case form of a character.

slides.caption: It returns an iterator because a few characters lower-case to several.
to_ascii_lowercase returns a single char, but only changes A–Z.

is_control.title: How char::is_control works
is_control.description: true for invisible control characters like newline and tab.

slides.caption: Control characters steer the output instead of showing a symbol.
Strip them from user input: s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()).

is_digit.title: How char::is_digit works
is_digit.description: true if the char is a digit in the given base.

slides.caption: In base 8 only 0–7 are digits; in base 16, a–f count too.

encode_utf8.title: How char::encode_utf8 works
encode_utf8.description: Writes the char's UTF-8 bytes into a buffer, without allocating.

slides.caption: A char needs 1 to 4 bytes; é needs 2.
It returns the written part as a &mut str. len_utf8() tells the size in advance.

len_utf16.title: How char::len_utf16 works
len_utf16.description: How many u16 units the char needs in UTF-16.

slides.caption: Characters beyond U+FFFF need a surrogate pair.
JavaScript string lengths count these units, so "🦀".length is 2 there.

is_ascii_punctuation.title: How char::is_ascii_punctuation works
is_ascii_punctuation.description: true for ASCII symbols such as ! ? , . - _

slides.caption: All printable ASCII symbols count; spaces do not.
Hex digits go up to f.

to_ascii_lowercase.title: How char::to_ascii_lowercase works
to_ascii_lowercase.description: The small version of A–Z; every other char is returned unchanged.

slides.caption: É is not ASCII, so it stays.
to_lowercase handles all alphabets but returns an iterator.

eq_ignore_ascii_case.title: How char::eq_ignore_ascii_case works
eq_ignore_ascii_case.description: Compares two chars, treating A and a as equal.

is_ascii_graphic.title: How char::is_ascii_graphic works
is_ascii_graphic.description: true for visible ASCII characters (no space, no control codes).

slides.caption: Letters, digits and symbols count; the space does not.
Useful to validate passwords or identifiers.

escape_unicode.title: How char::escape_unicode works
escape_unicode.description: The char written as \u{…} with its code point in hex.

slides.caption: Rust source accepts the same syntax: '\u{e9}' == 'é'.

is_ascii_alphabetic.title: How char::is_ascii_alphabetic works
is_ascii_alphabetic.description: true for a–z and A–Z only.

slides.caption: é is a letter, but not an ASCII one.
is_alphabetic accepts letters from every alphabet.
é is lowercase, but not ASCII.

is_ascii_whitespace.title: How char::is_ascii_whitespace works
is_ascii_whitespace.description: true for space, tab, newline, carriage return and form feed.

slides.caption: Unicode spaces such as the no-break space do not count.
Common for validating usernames or identifiers.
is_alphanumeric accepts every alphabet and digit system.

make_ascii_uppercase.title: How char::make_ascii_uppercase works
make_ascii_uppercase.description: Changes a char variable to its ASCII capital, in place.

slides.caption: to_ascii_uppercase returns a new char instead.
